mu_name_from: Object1/Bird01.bmd, which is not a placement. Nothing in lorencia.json refers to it: GOBoid.cpp keeps a pool of five in the air around whoever is playing and spawns them within a few tiles of the hero, so the bird exists only where somebody is looking. It is built like any other world model because it *is* one — a mesh, a sheet and an action — and the difference is only who decides where it goes. See Boids.
why_this_one: The town's only wildlife. 98 triangles and one 32x64 sheet, with a six-key wing beat in its own .bmd — the cheapest possible thing to have moving in an empty sky, and the difference between a town and a diorama of one.
sheet_from: Object1/bird.ozt, decoded rather than the Object12 copy of the same name — the client loads a model's textures out of the directory the model came from, and Bird01 is in Object1.
sheet_materials_from: Foliage, which is not a joke about feathers. What the material has to get right here is that this is a two-sided cut-out lit from both faces: a bird is a handful of alpha-keyed quads seen from underneath as often as from above, which is the same problem a leaf card poses and the reason foliage carries translucency. Skin and cloth are both opaque surfaces with a front and a back, and a bird wearing either goes black on the underside every time it banks.
cutout_from: The sheet is 32 by 64 with 37% of it cut away — the wings are shaped by alpha rather than by geometry, which is how MU draws anything with an outline.
